T: Have a cup of tea. Go to the pub. Wait for it to blow over.
D: A slacker in London tries to get his mum and girlfriend to safety during a zombie outbreak.
P: Serve the drinks when they make it to the Winchester.
S: Ed's hangover cure the morning after

Waffle cones dipped in chocolate and crushed nuts, filled with vanilla ice cream rippled with fresh strawberry sauce, a chocolate plug at the bottom. Simmer 250g strawberries with 60g caster sugar and a squeeze of lemon for 8 minutes, then cool. Melt 100g dark chocolate. Drop a spoon of chocolate into each of 4 waffle cones, then dip the rims in chocolate and in 40g crushed roasted hazelnuts. Set in the freezer 10 minutes. Soften 1L vanilla ice cream, ripple through the sauce and pack into the cones. Freeze 30 minutes before serving.
the pub, where everyone waits it out
Peanuts tossed in egg white, smoked paprika, salt and a little sugar, roasted at 160C for 15 minutes until crisp. Served in small bowls on the bar.
Shaun's walk to the corner shop, not noticing a thing
Thinly sliced potatoes fried at 170C until golden, tossed with salt and malt vinegar powder, or just salt and vinegar.
M: the Winchester's menu, if the kitchen's open
Steak and ale filling braised 2.5 hours, under a puff pastry lid, baked at 200C for 25 minutes, chips and mushy peas.

Bacon, pork sausages, fried eggs, baked beans, grilled tomato, buttery mushrooms, black pudding and toast, all on one big plate. Bake 8 pork sausages at 200C for 25 minutes. Fry 8 rashers bacon and 4 slices black pudding until crisp and keep warm. Halve 4 tomatoes and grill cut side up for 8 minutes. Fry 300g sliced mushrooms in 30g butter until golden. Warm 2 x 420g tins baked beans. Fry 4 eggs in the bacon fat until the whites set. Toast and butter 4 thick slices of bread and plate everything together.
W: a table Shaun forgot to book
Dates soaked with bicarb, beaten into a butter sponge, baked at 180C for 30 minutes, drowned in warm toffee sauce with cream.
K: wait for it all to blow over
English bitter or lager in a pint glass, cold, a toast to Ed.

edition.tagline: Have a cup of tea. Go to the pub. Wait for it to blow over.
edition.cue: Serve the drinks when they make it to the Winchester.

s.note: Crunchy smoked paprika peanuts in little bowls on the bar.
s.how: Whisk 1 egg white until frothy, then stir in 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp caster sugar. Toss through 300g peanuts, spread on a lined tray and roast at 160C for 15 minutes, stirring once, until crisp. Cool and serve in small bowls.

s.note: Thin homemade crisps with salt and malt vinegar.
s.how: Slice 600g potatoes paper thin on a mandoline, rinse well and dry completely. Fry at 170C in small batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain, sprinkle with sea salt flakes and splash with 2 tbsp malt vinegar.

m.note: Steak and ale pie with chips and mushy peas.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then soften 2 sliced brown onions. Add 330ml English ale, 300ml beef stock and 2 tbsp flour stirred in first, cover and braise at 160C for 2.5 hours. Cool slightly, tip into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with 1kg chips and 400g frozen peas cooked and crushed.

w.note: Date sponge drowned in warm toffee sauce with cream.
w.how: Soak 200g chopped dates in 250ml boiling water with 1 tsp bicarb soda for 10 minutes. Beat 80g butter with 150g brown sugar, add 2 eggs, fold in 180g self-raising flour and the dates. Bake in a greased dish at 180C for 30 minutes. Simmer 100g butter, 150g brown sugar and 200ml cream for 3 minutes and pour over. Serve with cream.

d.note: English ale or lager poured into pint glasses for a toast.
d.how: Chill four 500ml cans or bottles of English ale, or lager for anyone who prefers it. Pour into pint glasses at a tilt so the head settles, and raise them to the Winchester.
